characters.name: Valancy Stirling
characters.description: Protagonist; a shy, long‑suffering Stirling woman who lives a quiet life until she leaves home, marries, and finds freedom and love.

characters.name: Mrs. Frederick Stirling (Amelia)
characters.description: Valancy’s mother; a prim, controlling Stirling matron often called 'Mrs. Frederick'.

characters.name: Christine Stickles
characters.description: Valancy’s cousin who lives with Mrs. Frederick; nervous, gossipy, called 'Cousin Stickles'.

characters.name: Uncle Benjamin
characters.description: Wealthy, avuncular Stirling relative whose jokes and will influence family affairs.

characters.name: Uncle James
characters.description: Solemn Stirling elder; family oracle and moral censor who intervenes in crises.

characters.name: Aunt Wellington (Mary)
characters.description: Formidable, fashion‑conscious Stirling aunt (married to Uncle Wellington); named Mary in the narration.

characters.name: Uncle Wellington
characters.description: A Stirling elder; husband of Aunt Wellington and a social critic of lesser tolerance.

characters.name: Aunt Alberta
characters.description: A large, good‑natured Stirling aunt with a reputation for unselfishness.

characters.name: Uncle Herbert
characters.description: A Stirling relative; good‑humoured and kindly, host of an inclusive silver wedding.

characters.name: Aunt Mildred
characters.description: Competent, talkative Stirling aunt who prides herself on being capable.

characters.name: Aunt Isabel
characters.description: Sharp‑tongued Stirling aunt, censorious and critical of others.

characters.name: Cousin Georgiana
characters.description: Pious, prim Stirling cousin who frequently presages funerals and misfortunes.

characters.name: Cousin Gladys
characters.description: Stirling relative noted for complaining of 'neuritis' and for strong self‑opinion.

characters.name: Cousin Sarah Taylor
characters.description: Proper Stirling relation, noted for her pickle recipes and prudishness.

characters.name: Cousin Betty Stirling
characters.description: Stirling relation whose bridesmaid selections cause Valancy disappointment.

characters.name: Second Cousin Lilian
characters.description: Relation mentioned in family gossip regarding an approaching wedding.

characters.name: Second Cousin Geraldine
characters.description: Relative referenced in family lore for who was once 'given up' by doctors.

characters.name: Artemas Stickles
characters.description: Relative referred to in connection with a hair brooch (name occurs in text).

characters.name: Great-grandmother Stirling
characters.description: Ancestral Stirling ancestor referenced in family relics and motto.

characters.name: Frederick Stirling
characters.description: Valancy’s deceased father, remembered in family anecdotes.

characters.name: Amos Wansbarra
characters.description: Valancy’s maternal grandfather who chose her uncommon given name.

characters.name: Dr. H. B. Trent
characters.description: Gruff, outspoken Deerwood physician who initially examines Valancy and (by mistake) sends her a fatal letter.

characters.name: Dr. Ambrose Marsh
characters.description: Port Lawrence physician of the Stirling family’s choosing; married Second Cousin Adelaide Stirling.

characters.name: Rev. Dr. Stalling
characters.description: The rector whose stern finger chastises Valancy in childhood and who later attempts to bring her home.

characters.name: Mr. Towers
characters.description: Free Methodist minister who marries Valancy and Barney and holds simple services 'up back'.

characters.name: Mr. Bently
characters.description: Local Presbyterian minister referenced regarding Roaring Abel and local religion.

characters.name: Roaring Abel (Abel Gay)
characters.description: Nicknamed 'Roaring Abel'; a loud, eccentric, sometimes drunken islander who shelters Cecilia Gay and later befriends Valancy.

characters.name: Cecilia Gay
characters.description: Called 'Cissy' or 'Cecily'; a young woman who becomes ill and is nursed by Valancy until her death.

characters.name: Barney Snaith / Bernard Redfern / John Foster
characters.description: A complex central male figure: known locally as Barney Snaith (an outlawly islander), legally Bernard Redfern (son of Dr. Redfern), and published under the pen‑name John Foster; Valancy’s husband and companion.

characters.name: Dr. Redfern
characters.description: Industrialist and maker of Redfern remedies; father of Bernard (Barney); wealthy, genial industrialist figure.

characters.name: Tom MacMurray
characters.description: Former owner/builder of Barney’s island shack; his furnishings are in the Blue Castle.

characters.name: Banjo
characters.description: Barney’s large grey cat, affectionate and outspoken; a named animal connected to the Blue Castle.

characters.name: Good Luck
characters.description: Barney’s small tame cat (named 'Good Luck'), companion in the household.

characters.name: Leander
characters.description: A tame owl associated with Barney’s island household.

characters.name: Rachel Edwards
characters.description: An old housekeeper once employed by Roaring Abel; mentioned in his account of household troubles.

characters.name: Miss Clarkson
characters.description: Librarian in Deerwood who interacts with Valancy over books (John Foster’s works).

characters.name: Mr. Carewe
characters.description: Post‑office clerk at Deerwood who hands Valancy her letter from Montreal.

characters.name: Joe Hammond
characters.description: One of the clerks at Uncle Benjamin’s grocery store.

characters.name: Claude Bertram
characters.description: Clerk at Uncle Benjamin’s grocery store who snickers at Valancy early on.

characters.name: Mrs. Patterson
characters.description: Housekeeper for Dr. Trent (named as the doctor’s housekeeper who explains his sudden departure).

characters.name: Mrs. Judd
characters.description: Name of a woman mentioned in connection with Dr. Trent (appears in text as someone talking uptown); another housekeeper/neighbor figure.

characters.name: Connie Hale
characters.description: Young local woman encountered by Valancy in Lover’s Lane.

characters.name: Kate Bayley
characters.description: Young local woman encountered by Valancy in Lover’s Lane.

characters.name: Clayton Markley
characters.description: Man who built a pretty house for his bride Jennie Lloyd; mentioned by Valancy in envy.

characters.name: Jennie Lloyd
characters.description: Bride for whom Clayton Markley built a house; referenced as an object of Valancy’s envy.

characters.name: Will Desmond
characters.description: Man to whom Olive had been briefly engaged and who died; mentioned in backstory.

characters.name: Donald Jackson
characters.description: A man Olive had an affair with; mentioned in the family narrative.

characters.name: Cecil Price
characters.description: Olive’s fiancé (civil engineer), part of Olive’s romantic history.

characters.name: Rob Walker
characters.description: Young man mentioned in a dance episode and as a romantic interest of Valancy’s youth.

characters.name: Byron Stirling
characters.description: Relative (boy) who pinched Valancy in church at a childhood service incident.

characters.name: Margaret Blunt
characters.description: Host of a party Valancy attends; scene of Valancy’s humiliation at being overlooked.

characters.name: Ellen Hamilton
characters.description: Local woman discussed among the Stirlings in gossip.

characters.name: Edward Beck
characters.description: Widower of the Port road who later considers proposing to Valancy; a respectable older suitor.

characters.name: Mr. Bradly
characters.description: The minister (presbyterian) who conducts Cecilia Gay’s public funeral address.

characters.name: Rachel (old housekeeper)
characters.description: Name used for a beefed‑up old housekeeper in Roaring Abel’s anecdote (Rachel Edwards).

characters.name: Henry
characters.description: Dr. Redfern’s chauffeur (named in the scene at the river landing).

characters.name: Howard
characters.description: Son of Aunt Mildred mentioned in passing (child reference).

characters.name: Concluding/unnamed household animals (collective)
characters.description: Named household animals associated with Barney and the Blue Castle (listed individually above); included in narrative as companions.
